title: Aeneid, Book I — Proem & Invocation
author: Publius Vergilius Maro (Virgil)
source_notes: Latin text from the Oxford Classical Text tradition (Mynors); English translation by John Dryden, 1697.
reading_notes: The proem states the theme (arms and the man), names the scope (Troy to Italy and Rome), then invokes the Muse with a famous question: why does Juno pursue such a pious man? These opening lines are the template of epic statement of subject — imitated but rarely surpassed.

lines.original: Arma virumque cano, Troiae qui primus ab oris
lines.english: Arms, and the man I sing, who, forc'd by fate,
lines.gloss: Arma = 'arms, weapons' (accusative plural, object of cano); virum = 'man, hero' (accusative singular); -que = 'and'; cano = 'I sing' (1st singular present); Troiae = 'of Troy' (genitive singular); qui = 'who' (nominative singular); primus = 'first' (nominative); ab oris = 'from the shores' (ablative plural).

Italiam = 'to Italy' (accusative, place to which); fato = 'by fate' (ablative); profugus = 'exiled, a fugitive' (nominative); Lavinia = 'Lavinian' (adjective modifying understood 'shores'); venit = 'came' (3rd singular perfect).

lines.original: litora, multum ille et terris iactatus et alto
lines.english: Expell'd and exil'd, left the Trojan shore.
lines.gloss: litora = 'shores' (accusative plural); multum = 'much'; ille = 'that one, he' (refers to Aeneas); et... et = 'both... and'; terris = 'on the lands' (ablative plural); iactatus = 'tossed, buffeted' (past participle); alto = 'on the deep sea' (ablative).

lines.original: vi superum saevae memorem Iunonis ob iram;
lines.english: Long labors, both by sea and land, he bore,
lines.gloss: vi = 'by the force' (ablative); superum = 'of the gods above' (genitive plural, contracted from superorum); saevae = 'of savage, cruel' (genitive); memorem = 'mindful, remembering' (accusative, modifies iram); Iunonis = 'of Juno' (genitive); ob iram = 'because of the wrath' (accusative).

lines.original: multa quoque et bello passus, dum conderet urbem,
lines.english: And in the doubtful war, before he won
lines.gloss: multa = 'many things' (accusative plural neuter); quoque = 'also'; et = 'and, even'; bello = 'in war' (ablative); passus = 'having suffered' (deponent past participle of patior); dum conderet = 'until he might found' (subjunctive); urbem = 'a city' (accusative).

lines.original: inferretque deos Latio, genus unde Latinum,
lines.english: The Latian realm, and built the destin'd town;
lines.gloss: inferretque = 'and might bring in' (subjunctive); deos = 'gods' (accusative plural); Latio = 'to Latium' (dative); genus = 'race, stock' (nominative); unde = 'whence'; Latinum = 'Latin' (nominative singular neuter).

lines.original: Albanique patres, atque altae moenia Romae.
lines.english: His banish'd gods restor'd to rites divine,
lines.gloss: Albani patres = 'Alban fathers' (nominative plural); -que = 'and'; atque = 'and also'; altae = 'of lofty' (genitive, modifying Romae); moenia = 'walls' (nominative plural); Romae = 'of Rome' (genitive).

lines.original: Musa, mihi causas memora, quo numine laeso,
lines.english: Muse, tell me the causes; by what divinity slighted,
lines.gloss: Musa = 'Muse' (vocative); mihi = 'to me' (dative); causas = 'causes' (accusative plural); memora = 'recall, tell!' (imperative of memoro); quo numine = 'by what divine will' (ablative); laeso = 'offended, slighted' (ablative, participle of laedo).

lines.original: quidve dolens, regina deum tot volvere casus
lines.english: Or grieving at what, did the queen of the gods drive a man
lines.gloss: quidve = 'or at what' (neuter accusative + ve enclitic); dolens = 'grieving' (nominative participle); regina = 'queen' (nominative); deum = 'of the gods' (genitive plural, syncopated deorum); tot = 'so many'; volvere = 'to endure, roll through' (infinitive); casus = 'misfortunes, falls' (accusative plural).

lines.original: insignem pietate virum, tot adire labores
lines.english: Distinguished in piety, to face so many misfortunes,
lines.gloss: insignem = 'distinguished, marked out' (accusative, modifies virum); pietate = 'by piety, devotion' (ablative); virum = 'man' (accusative, refers to Aeneas); tot = 'so many'; adire = 'to approach, face' (infinitive of adeo); labores = 'labors, toils' (accusative plural).

lines.english: To undergo such trials? Can heavenly minds nurse such wrath?
lines.gloss: impulerit = 'drove, impelled' (3rd singular perfect subjunctive of impello); Tantaene = 'so great?' (nominative plural feminine + ne interrogative); animis = 'in minds' (dative plural); caelestibus = 'heavenly' (dative plural); irae = 'angers, wraths' (nominative plural).

lines.english: There was an ancient city (Tyrian colonists held it)
lines.gloss: Urbs = 'city' (nominative); antiqua = 'ancient' (nominative feminine); fuit = 'there was' (3rd singular perfect of sum); Tyrii = 'Tyrian' (nominative plural); tenuere = 'held' (3rd plural perfect, syncopated for tenuerunt); coloni = 'colonists' (nominative plural).

lines.english: Carthage, far opposite Italy and the mouths
lines.gloss: Karthago = 'Carthage' (nominative); Italiam contra = 'opposite Italy' (accusative + postposition); Tiberina = 'Tiberine, of the Tiber' (accusative plural neuter); -que = 'and'; longe = 'far off'.

lines.original: ostia, dives opum studiisque asperrima belli;
lines.english: Of the Tiber, rich in wealth and fiercest in the arts of war;
lines.gloss: ostia = 'mouths (of rivers)' (accusative plural); dives = 'rich' (nominative); opum = 'of resources' (genitive plural of ops); studiis = 'in pursuits, zeal' (ablative plural); -que = 'and'; asperrima = 'fiercest' (superlative of asper); belli = 'of war' (genitive).
